But in the genetic map (please see in the attachment), markers are overlapped in some points and I want to place the exact corresponding marker position (CM) in the left side.
Is there any option do to that using Rqtl?

Thank you very much.
Regards
Ishrat

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm trying to use MQM mapping on a RIL population of 178 lines with 1221 markers. On average my markers are about 1 cM apart.

I used mqmautocofactors() to select a set of 158 markers to be the cofactors. The number 158 comes from the number of lines minus 20.

> cofactors <- mqmautocofactors(mycross, num = nind(mydata1.argmax)-20, distance = 1, verbose = T)

The function outputs different sets of 158 cofactors every time I run the function. Here are 4 examples.

And when I used these sets of cofactors in mqmscan() I got LOD score peaks with different heights with different numbers of cofactors left in the model (ranging from 5 to 20 cofactors).

I suspect that the function mqmautocofactors() involve pseudorandom number generating algorithm because I got the same set of 158 cofactors when I used set.seed() to set the same seed before running mqmautocofactors() function.

My question is how do I report these results? Which LOD profile should I use? Or is it okay if I just randomly pick a seed for mqmautocofactor()?

Many thanks,
Nat
